title.narrative: Improvement of the security system of Caritas Goma in house and in the field

description.narrative: For over 20 years, North Kivu has continued to experience sporadic clashes between rival armed groups, making the work of humanitarian organizations difficult. Groups like FDLR, Raia Mutomboki, Mai Mai Mazembe, APCLS, Mai Mai Nyatura, … just to name a few, have remained operational in many areas of the North Kivu province. Currently, International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs), including CAFOD and Caritas Australia, have been implementing various humanitarian and development programmes through local organizations, including Diocesan Caritas. While INGO staff go through rigorous security training and have solid protocols, local organizations that remain on the front line in the field are left to struggle and only with survival mechanisms to maintain their security. Since 2016, Caritas Goma has experienced many forms of security incidences ie compound vandalised, armed robbery at the office, ambushes on the way to the field and recently their staff were kidnaped. Moreover, recently the clashes between armed groups during a food distribution in Mungote left two beneficiaries severely injured. In some other cases, beneficiaries of the humanitarian aids have seen their items taken by force by some unidentified armed men as they return from the distribution sites. All these have occurred due to inappropriate security assessment of zones of humanitarian intervention. Although Caritas Goma has made efforts to develop various security protocols, the implementation of the same remains a problem due to lack of proper equipment, training, analysis, and implementation of the security measures, the current project aims to support Caritas Goma to correct this. Caritas Goma has now recruited a trained security officer who has been tasked to provide timely security briefings to staff prior to their deployment in the field. The later participates in various platforms and meetings and has the possibility to liaise and triangulate with other organizations.
